Chapter 9: The Personal Cost of Public Service
You know, behind every headline... every policy, every diplomatic breakthrough... there are real people. People who give up time with their families, people who carry the weight of decisions they can never take back. The cost of public service? It's often invisible, but trust me—it's definitely real.
Picture this: nights spent alone in hotel rooms, miles away from home. Birthdays missed. Anniversaries celebrated through a phone screen. There's this constant pressure to always be on call, ready to jump into action when a crisis hits—no matter what time it is. And for some, the toll shows up physically—exhaustion, illness, the grind of nonstop travel. For others, it's emotional. That heavy knowledge that every choice you make... could change someone’s life.
Imagine one evening, after an especially grueling day, a diplomat sits quietly, gazing out over a city that never really sleeps. The phone, for once, is silent. That stillness? It's a relief, sure—but it also reminds them of everything they've given up. And in that quiet moment, a question sneaks in: is it all worth it?
There isn't a simple answer. Sometimes, there are doubts—moments of regret. But then come those moments of pride. When a tough deal finally goes through. When someone is saved. When a small act of kindness ripples out and matters in ways you never expected. For people who serve, this isn’t just a job. It’s a calling. The sacrifices? They’re real. But so are the rewards.
Over time, something becomes clear: self-care isn't optional. It's essential. Finding balance, leaning on friends and family, remembering that no one—no matter how dedicated—can do this work alone. Here’s the lesson: if you want to serve others, you’ve got to take care of yourself, too.
